The Data Term of a Multivariate t and Its Derivatives in nu

Source: R/mvstudent_t_distrib.R
mvt_h_d.Rd

Computes the \(k\)-th derivative in \(\nu\) of \(h = \tfrac{\nu+p}{2}\log(1 + q/\nu)\), the part of the log-density that carries the observation, at fixed \(q\). With \(u = q/\nu\) and \(a_k(u) = (1+u)^{-k} - 1\), for \(k \ge 2\) $$h^{(k)} = \tfrac{1}{2}(-1)^{k-1}(k-1)!\,\nu^{-(k-1)} \left\{B_k(u) + \tfrac{p}{\nu}\,a_k(u)\right\}, \qquad B_k(u) = a_k(u) - \tfrac{k}{k-1}\,a_{k-1}(u),$$ and \(h' = -\tfrac{1}{2}\{D(u) + (p/\nu)\,u/(1+u)\}\) with \(D\) from mvt_D().

Usage

mvt_h_d(u, nu, p, k)

Arguments

u

The ratio \(q/\nu\), a numeric vector.

nu

The degrees of freedom, a single positive number.

p

The dimension.

k

The order of the derivative, 1 to 4.

Value

A numeric vector as long as u.

Details

The two terms of \(B_k\) agree to first order in \(u\), so below \(u = 0.1\) it is summed as the power series \(\sum_{m \ge 2} (-1)^m\{\binom{k+m-1}{m} - \tfrac{k}{k-1} \binom{k+m-2}{m}\}u^m\), to \(m = 22\); above it the direct form loses at most one digit.

See also

mvt_cp_d() for the part that depends on \(\nu\) only; the derivative of the log-density in \(\nu\) only is \(c_p^{(k)} - h^{(k)}\).

Examples

# The result is compared with the direct form at nu = 1e9, where its terms
# cancel.
nu <- 1e9; q <- 1.25; p <- 2
h <- function(v) (v + p) / 2 * log1p(q / v)
distributions7:::mvt_h_d(q / nu, nu, p, 2L)
#> [1] 1.71875e-27
(h(nu * (1 + 1e-4)) - 2 * h(nu) + h(nu * (1 - 1e-4))) / (nu * 1e-4)^2
#> [1] -1.110223e-26
